discovery: Prediction of neutron-star mergers as sites of r-process nucleosynthesis and of their radioactively powered kilonova emission

nominees.name: Li-Xin Li
nominees.affiliation: Kavli Institute for Astronomy and Astrophysics, Peking University, China

subfield: Astrophysics / multi-messenger astronomy and nuclear astrophysics
motivation: Where the heaviest elements, such as gold and platinum, come from was a long-standing open question in physics. Lattimer (with Schramm) first proposed that neutron-rich matter ejected when a neutron star is tidally disrupted in a compact-binary merger undergoes rapid neutron capture. Li and Paczynski predicted that the radioactive decay of this ejecta would power a transient optical-infrared glow. Metzger and collaborators then calculated self-consistently, using nuclear heating rates, the luminosity and timescale of what they named the 'kilonova'. These predictions defined the electromagnetic counterpart searched for after GW170817. The observed kilonova AT2017gfo matched them closely. It established mergers as a major r-process site, constrained the dense-matter equation of state and enabled standard-siren cosmology. Their work turned gravitational-wave detections into a new multi-messenger laboratory for nuclear physics and the origin of the elements.
